# Itiha intelligence brief, 2026-11-25

**The Guru Tegh Bahadur date passed yesterday without its Short; the Goa shikha Short went up instead. Publish it by 26 November for search or press Drop. The Indonesia long-form is still adding subscribers every day, so its Bali follow-up is this week's main job, with the Churchill Short for 30 November.**

## This week: 3 decisions
1. **Script and publish a follow-up long-form for the Indonesia video's viewers: why Bali stayed Hindu when Java converted.** (long, due 2026-12-02, open since 2026-11-19)  
   Why: The Indonesia long-form has 112,678 views in 7 days and brings 3.9 subscribers per 1,000 views, against 2 for the Asia one. It still adds subscribers daily and is the nearest video to a breakout, so the follow-up should land while its viewers come. Bali is a guess from the comments.  
   First step: Add the Indonesia transcript to the long-form library today, so its drop-off can be read. Then read on Majapahit's fall, find the culprit and date for sentence one, and put Indonesia in the title.
2. **Script and publish a Short for Churchill's birthday on 30 November: what his War Cabinet was told about the Bengal famine in 1943, and what it decided.** (short, due 2026-11-30, open since 2026-11-24)  
   Why: Five days out, and this week is for recording it. A ruler's own papers on a famine that killed Indians is the shape of the video that brings the most subscribers per view in the last 90 days, “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”: a villain convicted by his own record. A British minister compared Zelensky to him this week, so the praise is in the news. It rests on the date and is a guess.  
   First step: Nothing is written. Read the 1943 War Cabinet minutes and Amery's diary today. Open on the document and its date, one line of context at most. Record by 28 November, or press Drop and record the Sati Short.
3. **Script and publish a Short on Aurangzeb's order to execute Guru Tegh Bahadur, for 24 November.** (short, due 2026-11-24, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: Overdue: the date passed yesterday with no Short. Late, it keeps only its search value. People look up “guru tegh bahadur history” all year, and the Gopal Patha Short, a named defender posted on his date, still draws views every day more than a year on. It will not close this month's breakout gap now.  
   First step: Decide today: write it now and publish by the evening of 26 November, title starting “Guru Tegh Bahadur”, Aurangzeb's order in sentence one; or press Drop. It lapses on its own on 27 November.

Everything below is the evidence. Mark a decision done or dropped on the Brief tab; an open one stays here until then.

## Channel health
18,300 subscribers, up 600 in a week, against 100,000 by 28 September 2027. November's milestone is 20,689, which needs 82 net a day. The last 7 days ran at 93.9, much of it from one video, the Indonesia long-form; the 28-day rate is 60.9. The channel is 1,947 behind the ramp, so on the 7-day rate November ends near 18,769, 1,920 short. Videos brought 50.6% of net subscribers over 28 days; the other 842 came with no video attached. Furthest behind is breakouts: 0 subscribers from them this month against 1,881 planned, and one video of the usual breakout size (1,396) closes most of it. Neither Ramayana long-form has crossed the breakout line of 500 subscribers yet; the Indonesia one is closest and still climbing, which is why the Bali follow-up comes first. Last week the long-form the owner chose beat the usual, the Short did not, and none of the brief's 58 picks shipped, so this week's dated Shorts lean on scripts already written.

What's working
- “How the Ramayana Was REWRITTEN to Convert Hindus” carried long-form: long-form views rose 91.1% week over week, and new long-forms have brought 658 subscribers this month against 104 planned. Over 28 days long-form earns 85.4% of the net subscribers videos bring.
- The video that brings the most subscribers per view in the 90-day window is “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, at 12.3 net per 1,000 views. Its lesson: “Name the villain, convict him with a document or payment he cannot deny, then end on who is still repeating him today.” The Churchill Short and the Bali video are both built on it.

What's wrong
- Long-form brings fewer subscribers per view than it used to: 7.3 per 1,000 over the 365-day window, now below its usual range. The three Ramayana long-forms bring 3.9, 2 and 1.1 per 1,000; only 41.7% of November's long-form views were engaged views, and the 7-day average view is 27.9%. Probable cause: most plays come from the Home feed and are not real viewing, and the stories with no culprit do not get followed. Test: the Bali video names a culprit and a date; compare its subscribers per 1,000 on day three with the Indonesia one's.
- Shorts views fell 83.2% week over week: 23,123 in the 7 days to 2026-11-22 against 137,582 the week before. Correction: yesterday's brief put this down to the Ramayana film losing screens; today's box-office news has it still earning on day 20 and entering India's top four. What stopped is the channel's own film Shorts: “Every Ramayana Kept One Rule. The Ramayana Movie BROKE It” (15 November) has 1,769 views against 79,092 for the one of 11 November. Probable cause: eight Ramayana Shorts between 30 October and 15 November, and the feed stops trying more of the same. Test: the Malay Ravana Short is the last one; if its first day is slower than the Goa shikha Short's 46.9 views an hour, no more film Shorts.
- Dated Shorts the brief asks for are not getting made: Tegh Bahadur missed its date and Tipu lapsed on 24 November, while the two Shorts that went up since 22 November, British officers' pay and the Goa shikha tax, were scripts already written. Probable cause: the brief kept picking dates with nothing on disk. Test: the next two dates, Sati on 4 December and Babri on 6 December, already have written scripts; see whether they ship.

## Audience
Analytics runs to 2026-11-22. Long-form is found on the Home and subscription feeds, 243,301 of its 272,080 views over 28 days against 6,929 from search, so a long-form's title and thumbnail must win on Home. Over 28 days the Shorts feed brought more Shorts views (152,678) than search (84,166), the reverse of the usual, because the film Shorts were pushed by the feed.
- Viewers in Indonesia are watching and writing in: “Hello from Indonesia! Watching this hit close to home because we are living through the exact implications of what you just explained.” One of them says Rama was never worshipped there in the Majapahit era, so the Bali script must check what Majapahit's court actually worshipped before it says anything about it.
- The most-liked objection under the Asia video is the Cholas: “Never sent a single soldier… ever heard of Chola Empire?”, and a second viewer asks about Rajendra Chola and Srivijaya. It is the first idea below.
- itiha.info: Google still finds the site only by its name, and November so far is thin ([Search Console](https://search.google.com/search-console?resource_id=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.itiha.info%2F)). Site visits cannot be read until the Analytics id is set (see actions).

## How they are reacting
The Indonesia long-form still holds the week's comments: viewers from Indonesia and Malaysia adding and correcting, a long fact-check, and anger turning on Islam as a whole. Under the Asia video the objection is the Cholas; under the Sai Pallavi Short it is still that she played Sita and defended Ravana.
- **Viewers in Indonesia and Malaysia, adding and correcting** (mixed): "This particular version of the Ramayana you are mentioning is a Malaysian adaptation known as the Hikayat Seri Rama"
- **The Asia video's “no army” line challenged** (mixed): "“Never sent a single soldier…” ever heard of Chola Empire?"
- **Anger turning on Islam as a whole** (negative): "Gaslighting since 1000 years ago... way to go islam."
- **Sai Pallavi playing Sita and defending Ravana** (negative): "The irony of playing Sita and defending Ravana in return"
- **Viewers abroad who grew up with the Ramayana** (positive): "I'm a Burmese and Buddhist from my home country Myanmar but still big fan of Ramayana"

Requested topics
- Rajendra Chola's raid on Srivijaya
- A Krishna video in the shape of the Asia Ramayana one
- Bagan and Hindu influence in Myanmar
- Hindi versions of the long-forms

## Competitors
The Ramayana film still drives the biggest Shorts on the watchlist, from channels much larger than Itiha. The one long-form among the month's top videos, Project SHIVOHAM's on Puri, opens the way the Bali video should.
- **Project SHIVOHAM**: "She's NOT Subhadra? The Forgotten Ancient Goddess"
  Why it worked: 262,269 views at 7.7x the channel's usual. It opens on a place millions have seen, gives the answer everyone holds (“Subhadra, the sister of Krishna and Balarama”), then breaks it: “But what if the answer is not so simple?”
  Steal: For Bali: open on the temple the viewer has seen in photos, the answer they already hold about why Bali is Hindu, then the dated act that breaks it.
- **Hindu Lifestyle**: "Diwali is South Asian... wait.. what?"
  Why it worked: 161,164 views at 30.9x the channel's usual, the top of the watchlist this month. It opens on the other side's claim in their own words, then one word: “What?”
  Steal: For Churchill: open on his admirers' line in their words (a British minister compared Zelensky to him this week), then put the War Cabinet's own record against it.
- **The Sham Sharma Show**: "Ranbir Kapoor as Parshuram was"
  Why it worked: 1,458,762 views at 9.9x his usual: a reaction to one character's scene in the Ramayana film, and the biggest film Short on the watchlist.
  Steal: Nothing for this week. The film still feeds Shorts on much larger channels; the channel's own film Shorts have stopped growing, so leave the film to them.

Gaps
- none

## Trending now, make this
- **today, short, 3/5**: Guru Tegh Bahadur, a day late  
  Signal: His date was 24 November and no Short went up. His name is no longer trending on X; the searched phrase “guru tegh bahadur history” stays all year. (Calendar, decision)  
  Make: Publish by the evening of 26 November or press Drop. Title starts with his name, Aurangzeb's order in sentence one, an act of state and not a martyr story.
- **this_week, short, 3/5**: Winston Churchill's birthday, 30 November  
  Signal: Five days out; recording is due this week. His English Wikipedia readership is at its usual level. A British minister compared Zelensky to him this week, so the praise is in the news. (Calendar, news, decision)  
  Make: Record by 28 November and publish the morning of 30 November, his name first in the title. One document, its date, then what was decided.
- **this_week, short, 3/5**: Bentinck bans sati, 4 December 1829  
  Signal: Nine days out, and a Short is already written and sourced, not recorded: “The Year Britain Banned Sati, Englishmen Were Selling Their Wives”. Under the channel's last sati Short, a liked comment made the same point: “People who burned witches in Europe stopped Sati in India”. (Calendar, script on disk, comments)  
  Make: Record by 2 December and publish the morning of 4 December. Before recording, settle the line the script itself flags: “never wrote a law” needs a source or softer wording.
- **this_week, short, 3/5**: 6 December: the Vishnu-Hari inscription  
  Signal: The second Ayodhya Short is written and waiting for the owner's edit: the slab that came out of the rubble on 6 December 1992, and the museum stone it was said to be. The first, “Irfan Habib’s Controversy: What the Court Record Actually Says #ThePrintIndia”, held viewers better than the channel's usual Short, 75.7% average view. (Calendar, script on disk)  
  Make: Edit it this week and publish the morning of 6 December, with pinned comments linking the two Shorts to each other. Keep it to the two stones and the dates.
- **watch, skip, 1/5**: The Ramayana film, day 20  
  Signal: Still earning: the box-office news has it entering India's top four. The channel's last film Short (15 November) has 1,769 views. (News, own Shorts)  
  Make: Skip new film Shorts. The Malay Ravana Short already written is the last one, because it sends viewers to the Indonesia long-form.
- **today, skip, 2/5**: 26/11, tomorrow  
  Signal: The 2008 Mumbai attacks are on the calendar for 26 November, beside Constitution Day. Nothing is written. (Calendar)  
  Make: Skip. A recap of news the audience already lived through gave the feed nothing to push here before (the Operation Sindoor video), and one day is not enough to find the angle nobody else has.

## Topic ideas (voltage-checked)
- [2/5, short] **Why Rajendra Chola Sent a Fleet to Srivijaya in 1025**  
  Contested history: the Asia video says the Ramayana spread without an army, and its most-liked objection is the Cholas; Empire mechanism: historians tie the raid to control of the sea route Indian merchants used to reach China; check this before scripting  
  source: Comments under “Why Does All of Asia Know the Ramayana?”. Made as a Short that hands viewers back to the Asia long-form. A guess: nothing on the channel has tested this subject.
- [3/5, long] **Churchill's War Cabinet and the Bengal Famine: The Minutes**  
  Extraction mechanism: what the War Cabinet decided about grain and shipping while Bengal starved; Villain plus hypocrisy: the wartime hero convicted by his own government's minutes; Decolonisation reframe: the famine told from the ruler's papers, not from Indian memory  
  source: Only if the 30 November Short beats the usual on day three. It follows the shape of the channel's best converter of the last 90 days, a villain convicted by his own record. A guess until the Short reports.

## Instagram (separate platform, separate audience)
Instagram has 25,550 followers, up 101 in 7 days, 14.4 a day. The latest reel, on British officers' pay, has reached 1,021, with 60.1% swiping away in the first three seconds, worse than the account's usual 54.0%. Carousels still do the growing: their median reach is 3.69x that of reels.

Do more
- Write carousels that correct the record  
  50 revision carousels in the band converted a median 53.5 followers against 20.5 for the other lanes (40 posts). Median reach 15.9k vs 10.9k, conversion 3.77 vs 1.95 per 1k. 490 followers a month at stake.
- Build every carousel at 7-10 cards  
  The median carousel in the 7-10 band converts 34.5 followers (90 posts); outside the band, 12 (16 posts). Pooled rate 2.89 vs 1.85 follows per 1k reach — the band is not just reaching more people, it converts better per person reached, so this is not a reach artefact. 429 followers a month at stake.

Do less
- Stop making posts that get shared without bringing followers  
  19 of 103 rated posts are shared above the median (24.6/1k) but convert below it (2.1/1k): median 8.5k reach for a median 8 followers. The 33 posts that do both average 283 followers each. Share rate and follow rate correlate at only 0.39 — shareable and followable are separate skills, and the first one flatters itself on the home screen. 1,034 followers a month at stake.
- Stop posting single images  
  87 single images all time: 84.3k reach between them and 120 followers, 1.4 per post. A carousel in the 7-10 band averages 159.6. Every image slot is a carousel slot not taken. 94 followers a month at stake.

## Housekeeping
- **now**: Upload the Malay Ravana Short today or tomorrow: title starting “Ravana”, Related video set to the Indonesia long-form, its link in the pinned comment, and the text named on screen as the Malay “Hikayat Seri Rama”.  
  It is written (19 November, from the owner's draft) and was built to send viewers to the Indonesia long-form while that video still draws them. Viewers there have already said this version is Malay. Whether a Short sends viewers on is a guess.
- **this_week**: Test a new title and the designer's thumbnail on “The Church That Ran Britain's PRISON Camps” in Studio's Test & Compare.  
  Over the 365-day window it brings 34.3 subscribers per 1,000 views, the best on the channel, on only 1,079 views: the people who find it subscribe, and too few find it. That the title is the reason is a guess.
- **later**: Check in Studio why “How Jati's evolve organically ?” still has 21 views since 3 November.  
  A public Short gets at least a few views a day; this points to a visibility setting or a restriction, not the topic.
- **later**: Set GA4_PROPERTY_ID in .env so the brief can read itiha.info's traffic.  
  Search Console alone is thin: every query that shows is the brand name.
